note: Reel 27: You're the Guard. Episode 5 of 'You're the test subject'. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart), talking to you, the guard. The four men (a01, b01, c01, d01) are placed from the cast reads. Script 2, after a fresh cold review: the first line points at the register, not his face (a face test primes people to study him); the register is why three walk; 'You're right' whichever you picked; 'and you carried on' is true for those who noticed; the last question has one fair answer on frame 0. Read audio/vo_lab/takes/phonemes.md after every run.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You're the guard, and what you write in this register sends a man to jail.
Flats on this street are being robbed, so ask this delivery man his name.
Ravi, sir.
Write it down, and ask which flat.
Three zero two.
Write that too, but anyone can say a flat number, so check his parcel.
Here it is, sir.
Does the label match your register?
It doesn't. Good catch.
Sorry, sir. I'll call the customer.
So nobody got past you.
Then who robbed flat three zero two?
Police have four men in that jacket, but your register says one came, so point him out.
He goes to jail, and the other three go home.
Which one? You looked right at him.
You're right. He was at your gate, and so were the other three.
Every time you looked down, one walked in and the next stepped up, and you carried on.
So three of them go home. Four, if you said none.
Psychologists once swapped a man in a hard hat for another, and one woman who missed it said she'd just seen a construction worker.
And these four aren't even delivery men. You just saw a jacket.
Your register says Ravi.
So which one was Ravi?
